headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia can forward-auth/OIDC with broad egress, while RisingWave has no egress and no shared workspace, so pairwise harms are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between Authelia and RisingWave. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth, but RisingWave has no IO surfaces or browser/subprocess behavior that would ingest Authelia output by default. With no bridge, prompt-injection pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, then injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not route Authelia outputs into RisingWave prompts or parsers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic, while RisingWave is documented as network-egress none. No sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, so leakage blast radius is small; however, if they share a workspace or credentials later, Authelia could transmit copied content outward.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace or secrets, then Authelia can exfiltrate copied material over the network.
IF RisingWave is configured to ingest sensitive files, then any copied content may be exposed through Authelia's egress.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Run Authelia and RisingWave under separate OS users.
Disable any manual file handoff between them.
Review outbound destinations for Authelia before enabling shared inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write or subprocess spawning, and RisingWave documents no network egress and no write-capable surfaces. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so a write/write or lock conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF RisingWave is later given filesystem or database write access, then overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared resources.
Avoid granting either agent git or database write access.
requires-engineering: add explicit locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions via OIDC/ForwardAuth, but RisingWave has no documented action-taking authority or input-verification pipeline. Without a documented downstream automation path, the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than default harmful action.
conditions: IF RisingWave is configured to act on Authelia-authored outputs without verification, then cascading error risk increases.
IF Authelia decisions are copied into operational workflows, then incorrect auth data could propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Authelia outputs.
Do not feed Authelia outputs directly into RisingWave jobs.
Add a verification step for any auth-derived data.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on exchanged records.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Authelia is open-source and RisingWave is open-source, but the profiles do not show a compliance mismatch or a single-agent residency violation, so no compliance pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, then a separate residency/certification review is required.
mitigations: Classify any data before routing it through either agent.
Keep regulated data out of this pair unless a policy review is completed.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls if regulated data is added.
